en.title: Daycare: first day
en.sub: Packing, paperwork, a countdown, a handout for teachers, and a goodbye that works
en.oneLiner: Short, warm, same every day — then leave. Xyla (~11 months, about to turn 1) is in peak stranger-anxiety age, so tears at drop-off are normal and usually stop soon after you go. Prep the bag and forms early so the last week is just about her.

labels.packHint: From the daycare's own list, plus what Xyla needs. Saved on this phone. Ticks are shared by both languages.
labels.papersHint: Some are already done (green). Tick the rest as you go.
labels.planHint: From two weeks out to the end of week one.
labels.aboutHint: Pre-filled with what we know. Fill the blanks, then print or save as PDF. What you type is saved on this phone only.
labels.aboutFoot: Tip: on iPhone, Print → pinch the preview → Share → Save to Files to get a PDF.
labels.byeHint: Tap a moment to see what to do and say.
labels.normalHint: Most of this is a sign she’s attached to you, not that something’s wrong.
labels.talkT: Talk to the teacher (or pediatrician) if…
labels.whyHint: Short notes from ZERO TO THREE and the AAP.

items.note: Tags of shirts, pants, socks, hats, coat. First + last name; unlabeled lost items usually get donated.

items.text: Stickers on water bottles and cups
items.note: Lid and body, both.

items.text: Label the crib sheet and blanket
items.note: Stamp the corner tag.
Sticker inside the tongue or heel.
Ask first; many daycares don't allow items from home.
Write on the pack itself.
The daycare asked for taped ones at this age. Start with a big pack.
Comes home Friday to wash, back Monday. A second set helps.
Long pants, tops, socks. Replace whatever comes home dirty.
Soft, flexible soles; easy for cruising.
Kids go outside daily, rain or shine. A one-piece rain suit + warm hat helps.
Original containers, labeled, with the daycare's medication form.
Home every day, washed, refilled with fresh water.
Good for wobbly first steps.

items.text: Her own cup for milk (if they want one)
items.note: Ask whether they use their cups or yours; straw or open cup, not a bottle.

items.text: Small family photo for her cubby
items.note: Ask the teacher; most love this.

items.text: Lovey or pacifier for nap — only if allowed
items.note: If not allowed, a T-shirt that smells like you can be an option to ask about.
Put them on the handout below.

items.text: Daycare app installed; both parents added
items.note: Turn on notifications.
Ask for any forms the daycare needs (annual physical) and get shots done.

items.text: Send the updated immunization record after the 12-month shots
Tell the daycare in writing: allergies, medical needs, diet
items.note: Even “no known allergies” is worth writing down. Allergy plans and meds must be in before day one.

items.text: Medication form for diaper cream / sunscreen (if sending)
Agree on milk: whole milk, formula, or both — and cup vs bottle
items.note: Tell the teacher where she is in the switch.

items.text: Check who's allowed to pick up (they'll need ID)
Confirm her age fits the class on day one
Send your questions to the daycare (list in the countdown)
Save the closure dates to your calendar
Line up backup care for sick days
items.note: She will catch colds; have a plan B and talk to work about flexibility.

items.text: Print “All about Xyla” and bring it to a visit

lines: Shop and label everything (stickers + stamp are ready).
Send your questions: milk type & cup, how they cut food for a 1-year-old, nap setup, lovey/pacifier, short first days, family photo.
Start the milk switch to whole milk from a cup around her birthday (see Milk at one), so she's not learning a new drink and a new place in the same week.
Practice short separations: 1–2 hours with a grandparent or sitter, using the same goodbye you'll use at daycare.
Book the 12-month checkup.
Naps: daycare usually has one midday nap. If she still naps twice, push the morning nap a bit later every few days. Car and stroller naps are short, so protect one real nap at home.
Practice falling asleep on her floor bed with her daycare sheet + blanket, so the smell is familiar.
Food: she's teething, so keep soft textures; offer soft chicken (her favorite) next to new foods. Practice finger foods and a cup at meals.
Talk about it in small doses: “You'll play at school, then Mama comes back.”
Fill in the handout; pick a goodbye song she loves to share with the teachers.
Stay with her. Sit on the floor and let her come back to you as her “safe base”.
Let the teacher play near her first before holding her — she warms up slowly.
Ask if you can drop off the labeled supplies on the last visit.
Ask how they'll update you on day one.
Bag by the door; outfit out; bottles washed and ready to fill.
Early bedtime. Keep the evening calm and boring.
Charge your phone; app notifications on.
Normal wake-up, normal breakfast, unhurried. Leave extra time.
Fill water bottles fresh.
Sing your daycare song in the car or stroller.
Sign in. Help her settle for a couple of minutes, then do the same quick goodbye (see below).
Hand her to a teacher, say goodbye, and leave. Never sneak out.
If she cries, that's okay. Don't come back in. Message the teacher 15–20 minutes later if you need to know.
Get down to her level: “Mama came back, like I said!” Big cuddle.
Take home bottles and dirty clothes; restock.
Quiet evening, early bed. Clinginess tonight is normal.
If the daycare allows, shorter days first (e.g. pick up after nap), then build up.
Same person, same time, same goodbye as much as you can.
Expect tiredness, more night waking, and her first cold. Keep weekends low-key.
Check in with the teacher at the end of week 1 and week 2.

plan.note: These steps are general advice; the daycare's own rules come first.

about.title: All about Xyla
about.intro: Hi! I'm Xyla. Here's how to help me feel at home.
about.foot: Made by Xyla's family. Thank you for taking care of me!

fields.label: My name
fields.value: Xyla

fields.label: Age
fields.value: About 12 months

fields.label: Words I say
fields.value: baba, mama, yeye (= grandpa in Mandarin), baibai (= bye-bye). I wave bye.

fields.label: Milk & drinks
fields.value: Formula now; switching to whole milk from a cup around my 1st birthday. Please no bottle at daycare unless we agree on it.

fields.label: Food
fields.value: I'm teething, so soft foods please, cut small. I love soft chicken. Allergies:

fields.label: Sleep
fields.value: At home I sleep on a floor bed. Car/stroller naps are short. Current naps:

fields.label: When I'm tired
fields.ph: e.g. rubs eyes, pulls ears, fussy, stares off

fields.label: When I'm hungry
fields.ph: e.g. fussy, reaches for food, smacks lips

fields.label: What comforts me
fields.value: Music! Singing to me works. Favorite songs:

fields.label: New people
fields.value: I warm up slowly. Play near me for a minute before picking me up.

fields.label: How I move
fields.value: Fast crawler. Pulls to stand, cruises, walks with a push walker, stands alone a few seconds. Climbs stairs up but can't go down safely yet. Slides down a slide alone.

fields.label: I love
fields.value: Music and songs, slides, push walker, playing next to other babies.

steps.do: Tell her the plan in toddler time, not clock time.
steps.say: Today is school. You play, eat, nap, then Mama comes back.

steps.do: Sing the same daycare song on the way. Same song every day.
Kneel, hug, eye contact. Keep your face and voice calm and happy.

steps.say: Mama loves you. After nap, Mama comes back. Baibai!

steps.do: Wave together (she knows “baibai”). Hand her to a teacher.
Walk out. Don't sneak away, and don't come back for one more hug.

scripts.note: Same words, same order, every day. That predictability is what helps.

steps.do: Stay calm. Name it once.
steps.say: You're sad. Mama always comes back.

steps.do: Hand her to the teacher and go. Lingering makes it longer.
Message the teacher 15–20 minutes later if you need to know. Most babies settle soon after the parent leaves.
Get down to her level and open your arms.
steps.say: Mama came back, like I said!

steps.do: Let her cling or cry; it's relief. Skip the questions and give her a calm evening.

normal.title: Crying at drop-off
lines: Separation anxiety peaks between 12 and 24 months — right when she starts.
Crying at the door is not a sign the daycare is wrong. What matters is that she settles and plays after you leave. Ask the teacher how long it took.

normal.title: Extra clingy at home
lines: She may cry when you leave the room, want to be held, or melt down after pickup. She held it together all day; now she's safe with you.
Give extra cuddles and keep routines the same.

normal.title: Tired, sleep changes
lines: Daycare naps can be short at first. Early bedtime for a few weeks helps.
More night waking is common and usually fades.

normal.title: Lots of colds
normal.sub: The first year is the worst
lines: The AAP says babies who start group care may get as many as 8–12 more colds in the first year than babies at home. It gets better in the second year.
Runny nose and cough without fever is often OK for daycare; fever, vomiting or diarrhea usually means home. Your daycare's sick policy decides.

normal.title: Eating or drinking less there
lines: New place, new cup, new food. Offer a good breakfast and dinner.
If she barely drinks there for several days, tell the teacher.

normal.title: Backsliding after a break
lines: Drop-off can get hard again after time off. Same goodbye, and it passes again.

talk: She's still crying hard most of the day after 3–4 weeks, or never seems to settle and play.
She's not eating or drinking at daycare for several days, or not napping at all.
Big changes at home (sleep, mood, eating) last more than 2–3 weeks.
You're unsure how food is cut for her (choking risk) or how naps are done.
Any injury or bite, or anything that just feels off to you.
Call the pediatrician for fever, trouble breathing, signs of dehydration, or anything that worries you.

why.title: Secure attachment = she protests, then trusts
lines: Babies around this age understand that when you leave, you go somewhere they can't follow — so they protest.
With a routine, she learns that you come back, every time, and learns to keep you in mind while you're gone.

why.title: Why not sneak out
lines: Sneaking away makes a child worry you might disappear at any time, which makes separation anxiety worse.
AAP: once you've left, don't reappear unless you're ready to stay.

why.title: Why short and the same every day
lines: The AAP's advice: a quick goodbye ritual, done the same way at the same time. If you linger, the anxiety lasts longer too.
Practicing short separations before daycare helps.

refs.label: AAP: How to ease separation anxiety

why.title: Visits and a reminder of home
lines: Visit together first and show her you like and trust the teacher.
A family photo or something that smells like you can help — ask what the daycare allows.

refs.label: AAP: Preparing your child for child care
CA Dept. of Education: The first days

why.title: Germs and when to stay home
lines: Lots of illness in the first year of group care is expected; immune systems catch up.
Fever with symptoms, vomiting 2+ times, or diarrhea usually means home. Follow your daycare's policy, which may be stricter.

refs.label: AAP: When to keep your child home
AAP: Reducing illness in child care

why.title: Milk at one
why.sub: See the Milk at one page
lines: Whole milk from a cup starting at 12 months is the AAP's general advice. Coordinate the switch with what the daycare serves.
→ Milk at one

zh.title: 上托班第一天
zh.sub: 打包、表格、倒计时、给老师的小卡片，还有不哭（少哭）的告别
zh.oneLiner: 告别要短、要暖、每天都一样——然后就走。Xyla 现在 11 个月左右，快一岁了，正是最认生的时候，门口哭很正常，一般你走了没多久就好了。包和表格早点弄好，最后一周就只管陪她。

labels.packHint: 照着托班自己给的清单，再加上 Xyla 需要的。勾选会存在这台手机上，中英文共用。
labels.papersHint: 有些已经搞定了（绿色），剩下的边做边勾。
labels.planHint: 从提前两周到第一周结束。
labels.aboutHint: 已经填好我们知道的，空的地方你补上，然后打印或存成 PDF。你写的内容只存在这台手机上。
labels.aboutFoot: 小技巧：iPhone 上点打印 → 两指放大预览 → 分享 → 存储到“文件”，就是 PDF 了。
labels.byeHint: 点开每个时刻，看该做什么、说什么。
labels.normalHint: 这些大多说明她跟你感情好，不是出了问题。
labels.talkT: 遇到这些情况，找老师（或儿科医生）聊聊：
labels.whyHint: 来自 ZERO TO THREE 和美国儿科学会（AAP）的简短说明。

items.note: 上衣、裤子、袜子、帽子、外套的标签上都盖。要写全名，没名字的东西丢了一般就被捐掉了。
杯盖和杯身都贴。
在角上的标签盖章。
贴在鞋舌或鞋跟里面。

items.text: 安抚奶嘴 / 安抚玩偶贴名字（允许带才贴）
items.note: 先问清楚，很多托班不让带家里的东西。

items.text: 尿布包、湿巾、护臀膏都写上名字
items.note: 直接写在包装上。

items.text: 粘贴式纸尿裤（不要拉拉裤）
items.note: 托班说这个年纪要粘贴式的，先备一大包。
每周五带回家洗，周一带回去。备两套更省心。
长裤、上衣、袜子。弄脏带回来的要记得补上。
软底、能弯，扶走方便。
每天都要去户外，下雨也去。连体雨衣加保暖帽很实用。
用原包装、贴好名字，再填托班的用药表。
每天带回家洗干净，第二天装新鲜的水。
刚学走路的时候更稳。

items.text: 她自己的牛奶杯（如果托班需要）
items.note: 问一下用托班的杯子还是自己带；吸管杯或敞口杯，不用奶瓶。

items.text: 一张小小的全家福，放她的格子里
items.note: 问问老师，大多数都很欢迎。

items.text: 午睡用的安抚玩偶或奶嘴——允许才带
items.note: 如果不让带，可以问问能不能放一件有你味道的 T 恤。

items.text: 写下她最喜欢的几首歌
items.note: 写到下面的宝宝卡里。

items.text: 托班 App 装好了，爸爸妈妈都加上了
items.note: 记得打开通知。
顺便问医生要托班需要的表（每年一次的体检表），该打的针打上。

items.text: 打完一岁的针，把更新后的疫苗记录发给托班
书面告诉托班：过敏、身体情况、饮食要求
items.note: 就算“没有已知过敏”也写下来。过敏方案和药要在第一天之前交。

items.text: 如果带护臀膏 / 防晒霜，填用药表
和老师说好喝什么奶：全脂奶、配方奶还是都有——用杯子还是奶瓶
items.note: 告诉老师她转奶转到哪一步了。

items.text: 决定要不要签拍照授权
确认谁可以来接（要带证件）
确认第一天她的年龄符合这个班
把问题发给托班（倒计时里有清单）
安排好生病时的备用照顾
items.note: 肯定会感冒，提前找好备胎，也和公司聊聊弹性上班。

items.text: 打印“宝宝介绍卡”，去试园时带上

lines: 买齐东西，全部贴好名字（姓名贴和印章已经有了）。
把问题发给托班：喝什么奶、用什么杯子、一岁宝宝的饭怎么切、午睡怎么安排、能不能带安抚物、头几天能不能早接、能不能放全家福。
一岁前后开始转全脂奶，用杯子喝（看“一岁转牛奶”那页），别让她同一周既要适应新奶又要适应新地方。
练习短时间分开：让爷爷奶奶或保姆带 1–2 小时，用的告别方式跟去托班一样。
约好一岁体检。
午睡：托班一般只有中午一觉。如果她还睡两觉，每隔几天把上午那觉往后挪一点。车上、推车里睡得都短，家里至少保一觉睡踏实。
让她在地床上铺托班那套床单和小被子练习入睡，先熟悉味道。
吃饭：她在长牙，吃软一点的；新食物旁边放点她最爱的软鸡肉。吃饭时练练手指食物和杯子。
一点点跟她说：“你去学校玩，玩完妈妈就来接你。”
填好宝宝卡；挑一首她最喜欢的告别歌，告诉老师。
全程陪着。坐在地上，让她玩一会儿就回来找你——你就是她的“安全基地”。
让老师先在她旁边玩，别急着抱，她慢热。
问问最后一次试园能不能把贴好名字的东西先放过去。
问问第一天老师会怎么跟你同步情况。
包放门口，衣服摆好，水杯洗好等着装水。
早点睡。晚上安安静静的，别安排新花样。
手机充满电，App 通知打开。
照常起床、照常吃早饭，别赶。多留点时间。
水杯装新鲜的水。
路上唱你们的“上学歌”。
签到。陪她熟悉两三分钟，然后用每天一样的快速告别（看下面）。
把她交给老师，说拜拜，然后就走。千万别偷偷溜。
她哭也没关系，别再回去。实在不放心，15–20 分钟后给老师发个消息问问。
蹲下来跟她平视：“妈妈说会回来，真的回来啦！”抱一大抱。
水杯、脏衣服带回家，缺的补上。
晚上安静点，早点睡。今晚特别黏人很正常。
托班允许的话，头几天早点接（比如午睡后），再慢慢加长。
尽量同一个人送、同一个时间、同一种告别。
她会更累、夜醒多，第一次感冒也可能来了。周末别安排太满。
第一周和第二周结束时，各找老师聊一次。

plan.note: 以上是通用建议，以托班自己的规定为准。

about.title: Xyla 宝宝介绍卡
about.intro: 你好！我是 Xyla，这样照顾我，我会更快适应哦。
about.foot: Xyla 的家人做的。谢谢你照顾我！

fields.label: 我叫
fields.value: Xyla

fields.label: 年龄
fields.value: 一岁左右

fields.label: 我会说的词
fields.value: baba（爸爸）、mama（妈妈）、yeye（爷爷）、baibai（拜拜），会挥手说再见。

fields.label: 喝奶
fields.value: 现在喝配方奶；一岁前后改喝全脂奶，用杯子喝。在托班先别用奶瓶，除非我们商量好。

fields.label: 吃饭
fields.value: 在长牙，请给软一点的、切小块。最爱软软的鸡肉。过敏：

fields.label: 睡觉
fields.value: 在家睡地床。车上、推车里睡得很短。现在每天睡：

fields.label: 我困了会
fields.ph: 比如：揉眼睛、抓耳朵、闹、发呆

fields.label: 我饿了会
fields.ph: 比如：哼哼唧唧、伸手要吃的、咂嘴

fields.label: 怎么哄我
fields.value: 音乐！给我唱歌最管用。最爱的歌：

fields.label: 见到新面孔
fields.value: 我比较慢热。先在我旁边玩一会儿，再来抱我。

fields.label: 我的大运动
fields.value: 爬得飞快。会扶站、扶走，推着学步车能走很多步，能自己站几秒。会往上爬楼梯，但还不会安全地下来。能自己滑滑梯。

fields.label: 我喜欢
fields.value: 音乐和唱歌、滑滑梯、学步车、在别的宝宝旁边玩。

fields.label: 还想说的
fields.ph: 老师需要知道的其他事

steps.do: 用宝宝听得懂的顺序讲，别讲几点几分。
steps.say: 今天去学校哦。玩一玩、吃饭饭、睡觉觉，然后妈妈就来接你。

steps.do: 路上唱同一首“上学歌”，每天都唱这首。
蹲下、抱一抱、看着她的眼睛。表情和声音放轻松、开心一点。

steps.say: 妈妈爱你。睡完觉，妈妈就来接你。拜拜！

steps.do: 一起挥手（她会说“拜拜”）。把她交给老师。
转身走。别偷偷溜，也别回头再抱一下。

scripts.note: 每天同样的话、同样的顺序。就是这种可预期，才让她安心。

steps.do: 你先稳住，帮她说出来一次。
steps.say: 你舍不得妈妈，难过了。妈妈一定会回来的。

steps.do: 交给老师，然后走。越磨蹭，哭得越久。
不放心的话，15–20 分钟后给老师发消息问问。大多数宝宝爸妈一走没多久就不哭了。
蹲下来张开手臂。
steps.say: 妈妈说会回来，真的回来啦！

steps.do: 她黏着你或者哭一下都没关系，那是松了口气。别追着问，晚上安安静静过。

normal.title: 送的时候哭
lines: 分离焦虑在 12–24 个月 最厉害——她正好这时候入园。
门口哭不代表托班不好。关键是你走了以后她能不能平静下来去玩。问问老师她多久就好了。

normal.title: 在家特别黏人
lines: 你一离开房间她就哭、要抱，或者接回来就崩溃。她在外面撑了一天，回到你身边才敢放松。
多抱抱，家里的作息别变。

normal.title: 累，睡觉有变化
lines: 刚开始托班的午睡可能很短。头几周早点哄睡。
夜里醒得多也常见，一般会慢慢好。

normal.title: 老是感冒
lines: AAP 说，婴儿期开始上托班的孩子，第一年可能比在家带的孩子 多感冒 8–12 次。第二年就会少很多。
只是流鼻涕、咳嗽、不发烧，通常可以去；发烧、吐、拉肚子一般就得在家。具体听托班的规定。

normal.title: 在托班吃得少、喝得少
lines: 新地方、新杯子、新饭菜。早饭、晚饭在家吃好点。
如果连着几天在托班几乎不喝水，告诉老师。

normal.title: 休息几天后又哭了
lines: 放完假送园可能又变难。还用一样的告别，过几天又会好。

talk: 过了 3–4 周，她大半天都还在哭，或者一直没法安顿下来玩。
连着几天在托班不吃不喝，或者完全不睡午觉。
家里的睡眠、情绪、吃饭变化超过 2–3 周还没好。
你不确定老师怎么给她切食物（怕噎着），或者午睡怎么安排。
受伤、被咬，或者你就是觉得哪里不对劲。
发烧、呼吸困难、有脱水迹象，或者任何让你担心的情况，直接找儿科医生。

why.title: 安全依恋：先抗议，再信任
lines: 这个月龄的宝宝已经明白：你走了，是去了一个她跟不过去的地方——所以会抗议。
有了固定的流程，她慢慢学会妈妈每次都会回来，你不在的时候她心里也装着你。

why.title: 为什么不能偷偷溜
lines: 偷偷走会让孩子担心你随时会消失，分离焦虑反而更重。
AAP：已经走了就别再出现，除非你打算留下来。

why.title: 为什么要短、要每天一样
lines: AAP 的建议：告别仪式要短，每天同一时间、同一种方式。你磨蹭多久，她焦虑就拖多久。
入园前先练习短时间分开，会有帮助。

why.title: 先试园，带点“家的味道”
lines: 先一起去看看，让她看到你喜欢、信任老师。
全家福或者有你味道的东西会有帮助——先问托班允许带什么。

refs.label: 加州教育厅：入园头几天

why.title: 细菌和什么时候该在家
lines: 上托班第一年生病多是正常的，免疫力会慢慢跟上。
发烧加其他症状、吐两次以上、拉肚子，一般就在家休息。以托班规定为准，可能更严。

refs.label: AAP：什么时候该让孩子在家

why.title: 一岁转牛奶
lines: AAP 的一般建议是 12 个月起用杯子喝全脂奶。转奶的节奏和托班提供的奶配合好。
→ 一岁转牛奶
